title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's study of pairs (σ, ρ) in GL(2) over an arbitrary base scheme S. Their images σ̃, ρ̃ in PGL(2) are tied to the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets). The target relations are σ̃² = ρ̃³ = 1, i.e. the presentation of PSL₂(ℤ) = ℤ/2 * ℤ/3 and its central extensions (B₃, SL₂(ℤ)).

Earlier sections (IV, V and formulas (6), (11)) put the pair into a normal form with parameters v, v', w, w' satisfying v + v' = 0 and w + w' = 1. From (21) and (12) one infers σ = [[0,-1],[v',w']] and ρ = [[0,1],[v,w]]. Then Tr σ = w', Tr ρ = w, det σ = v', det ρ = -v.

Condition 2°) is from the previous page: Tr σ = 0, equivalently w' = 0, w = 1, σ̃² = 1, σ² = v'·id. This page records the resulting normal form (19): σ = [[0,-1],[v',0]], ρ = [[0,1],[v,1]] with v + v' = 0.

Grothendieck then comments on method. Parts 1°) and 2°) only recapitulate part of sections IV and V. The new step is to study conditions that pin down w (equivalently w') explicitly, and conditions that pin down v (equivalently v') explicitly.

Condition 3°), formula (20): det σ = 1 ⇔ det ρ = 1 ⇔ v = -1 ⇔ v' = 1 ⇔ ε₀ = [[1,-1],[0,1]], with ε₀ the element defined in (6). The equivalent normal form (21) is σ = [[0,-1],[1,w']], ρ = [[0,1],[-1,w]] with w + w' = 1.

Check on the reduced form (19): σρ = [[-v,-1],[0,v']] = [[-v,-1],[0,-v]]. For v = -1 this equals the unipotent [[1,-1],[0,1]], consistent with the claimed equivalence to ε₀ = [[1,-1],[0,1]].

Condition 4°) begins at the bottom of the page and continues overleaf. It is the conjunction of 2°) and 3°): σ² = -1 and σ̃² = ρ̃³ = 1. This forces σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]] and ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]], the standard order-4 and order-6 generators of SL₂(ℤ).

Purpose. The page is a lattice of equivalent normalizations: trace conditions fix w, w' and determinant conditions fix v, v'. Together they cut out, scheme-theoretically over S, the locus where the pair is the standard SL₂(ℤ) pair.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. All stated equivalences follow from det σ = v', det ρ = -v, v + v' = 0 in the normal form.

Minor: the form (21) agrees with the general normal form only if the general σ, ρ have the shape [[0,-1],[v',w']], [[0,1],[v,w]], which is not displayed on this page. The identification of ε₀ with [[1,-1],[0,1]] depends on definition (6), not shown here.

ideas.what: Normal forms for pairs (σ, ρ) in GL₂ over a base scheme whose PGL₂-images satisfy σ̃² = 1 and ρ̃³ = 1, parametrised by v, v', w, w' with v + v' = 0, w + w' = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli/representation scheme of 2-dimensional representations of B₃ / PSL₂(ℤ) = ℤ/2*ℤ/3 (character variety of the modular group).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (SL₂(ℤ) generators); representation varieties of B₃ studied e.g. by Tuba–Wenzl (low-dimensional B₃ representations).
ideas.where_published: Not published; related themes (Teichmüller tower, PSL₂(ℤ), loop relations) in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche, but not these computations.

ideas.what: Determinant conditions det σ = 1 ⇔ det ρ = 1 ⇔ v = -1 fix the product to a standard unipotent and reduce to SL₂.
ideas.modern_name: Standard generators S = [[0,-1],[1,0]], ST-type [[0,1],[-1,1]] of SL₂(ℤ).

deep.surprise_reason: Routine 2×2 matrix bookkeeping: a recapitulation and normalization step in a longer scheme-theoretic study of PSL₂(ℤ)/B₃-type pairs. No new result or connection on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: The garbled sentence reads roughly: 'Ici, il s'agit d'étudier des conditions qui reviennent à la détermination de la valeur de w (ou encore de w') de façon très explicite. Puis on va trouver aussi des conditions qui doivent revenir à fixer v (ou encore v') de façon explicite.' 'très' is not deleted; the deleted words are 'Ici' and 'dans'.
In (21) the σ is written over a crossed-out ρ.
Under v' in (19) is written '= -v' (vertical equality sign), i.e. v' = -v.
